headlines.title: 美·이 란 전쟁에 더 커진 재정 불안 … 한국도 국가신용등급 강등 우려
headlines.summary: 국고채·외평채 금리 판단 기준 수년간 안정세… 상반기 재산정 미국·이란 전쟁 장기화 우려로 9일 환율이 급등하고 주가는 곤두박질치는 금융위기급 쇼크가 발생함에 따라 한국의 국가신용등급 변화에 대한 우려도 커지고 있다. 지난해 미국·중국·프랑스 등은 재정 우려로 국가신용등급이 줄강등됐는데 대외 변동성이 큰 한국에 대한 평가가 달라질지 주목된다.

headlines.title: 중동전쟁에 고용쇼크 까지… 美 금리 인하 기대감 ' 뚝 '
headlines.summary: 미국과 이스라엘의 이란 전쟁에 미국의 기준금리 인하 가능성이 점차 떨어지고 있다. 국제유가가 높아지고 있는 데다 미국의 고용 사정도 악화하면서 스태그플레이션이 찾아올 수 있다는 우려가 점차 힘을 얻고 있다. 이로 인해 올해 1~2회 인하하는 것도 쉽지 않을 것이라는 전망이 나온다. 기존에는 2~3회 인하를 예상했다.

headlines.title: 서울부동산 ‘ 큰손 ’ 된 30대 생애 최초·경매까지 장악
headlines.summary: 1~2월 생애최초 매수자 53% 차지 경매 시장서도 30대 낙찰 비중 1위 집값상승·정책대출 영향 매수 확대 서울 부동산 시장에서 30대들이 ‘큰 손’으로 떠오르고 있다. 생애최초 주택매수자 가운데 30대가 과반을 차지한 가운데 경매 시장에서도 30대 낙찰자 비중이 가장 높았다.

headlines.title: “ 15억 넘으면 못 사 ”…강북 일대 아파트 구매 ‘ 속도전 ’

headlines.title: 다주택자 주담대 373조 …1년 새 36조 증가

key_headlines.title: S&P to Conduct Annual Review of Korea's Sovereign Credit Rating
key_headlines.summary: Standard & Poor's is visiting Korea from March 9-11 for annual consultations to assess the nation's economic conditions, monetary, and fiscal policies. The review's outcome, determining Korea's credit rating, is expected in the first half of the year.

key_headlines.title: Oil Prices Breach $110, Won-Dollar Exchange Rate Nears 1500
key_headlines.summary: Global oil prices, including Brent crude, surged past $100 and then $110, driven by the Middle East crisis and the official selection of Iran's new leader Mojtaba. This surge is pushing the won-dollar exchange rate towards a critical 1500 KRW, causing panic in financial markets.

key_headlines.title: Oil Shock Triggers KOSPI Circuit Breaker, Exchange Rate Nears 1500
key_headlines.summary: The escalating Middle East conflict led to a severe market shock in Korea, with WTI crude prices exceeding $100 for the first time since July 2022. The KOSPI index plummeted, triggering a circuit breaker for the second time this month, while the won-dollar exchange rate surged to 1496 KRW, marking its highest level since the financial crisis.

key_headlines.title: Global Stock Markets Anticipate Further Corrections
key_headlines.summary: Following a volatile week, global stock markets are expected to undergo additional adjustments in the short term, despite a late recovery in New York's major indices due to bargain hunting. Initial fears over the Euro crisis had caused sharp declines before the rebound.

key_headlines.title: Experts Forecast 35% Probability of US Recession This Year Amid Oil Shock
key_headlines.summary: Economic forecasts and market experts are increasingly aligning on a significant 35% probability of a U.S. recession this year. This concern stems from persistent inflation driven by oil supply shocks, which unlike demand-side inflation, directly hinders economic growth and forces the continuation of high interest rate policies.

sections.Hot Economy News: The Korean economy faces a "perfect storm" as S&P conducts its annual credit rating review amid an escalating global energy crisis. Oil prices breaching $110 and the won-dollar exchange rate threatening 1500 KRW/USD have triggered a panic in financial markets, leading to a KOSPI circuit breaker. President Lee is convening an emergency economic meeting to address the Middle East situation and ensure stable oil and gas supplies. Global stock markets are bracing for further corrections, reflecting widespread concern over the economic fallout.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Experts forecast a 35% probability of a U.S. recession this year, primarily due to inflation spurred by oil supply shocks, which negatively impacts economic growth. China is also experiencing its largest inflation surge in three years, raising concerns about stagflation due to the Strait of Hormuz blockade leading to raw material shortages. High oil prices pose a significant dilemma for the Bank of Korea, caught between curbing inflation with rate hikes and stimulating the economy with cuts, while a 10% jump in oil prices is projected to reduce Korean exports by 0.39%.
sections.Financial Markets: The Korean financial market experienced a "Black Monday" due to the Middle East geopolitical risks, with the KOSPI index plummeting by 6% and triggering a circuit breaker. The won-dollar exchange rate surged to 1495 KRW, nearing 1500 KRW and reaching its highest point since the global financial crisis, while bond prices also fell, leading to a "triple crunch" (high oil, high exchange rate, high interest rates). The Bank of Korea stated it would take appropriate market stabilization measures if excessive volatility continues. Global bond markets are also shaking, with U.S. 10-year Treasury yields rising for six consecutive days.
sections.Industry & Technology: The "InterBattery 2026" exhibition showcased advanced battery technologies beyond electric vehicles, expanding into robots, drones, and Energy Storage Systems (ESS) to diversify amid the EV "chasm." Samsung SDI unveiled samples of solid-state batteries for "physical AI" applications like humanoid robots, aiming for mass production by late 2027. Meanwhile, the "perfect storm" of surging oil prices and exchange rates is threatening Korea's key industries, including semiconductors and automobiles, raising fears of a potential energy shock worse than the 1970s oil crisis if global consumption weakens.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's new apartment rental market is rapidly shifting towards monthly rent (wolse), with 60% of new contracts being monthly or semi-monthly, due to stricter government regulations on jeonse (lump-sum deposit) loans. A Seoul mayoral candidate has pledged to accelerate urban redevelopment and reconstruction projects through a "chak-chak planning" system and combat jeonse fraud. While apartment prices in Gangnam, Seocho, and Songpa districts are declining, Yongin Suji in Gyeonggi Province is experiencing a rapid price increase, defying the trend and setting new highs, driven by local factors. Current interest rates and DSR regulations continue to limit housing purchase power for many.
sections.International Economy: The Middle East conflict, particularly the Iran situation, is causing global panic in financial markets due to soaring oil prices and the threat of a third oil shock. This has heightened inflation concerns, prompting speculation that the U.S. Federal Reserve might limit interest rate cuts to only one or two times this year, rather than the previously anticipated multiple cuts. Russia is reportedly benefiting from the Middle East instability by selling oil and impacting European economies. The Fed's upcoming FOMC meetings are critical for determining future rate policy amidst these global challenges.
sections.AI & Economy: Nobel laureate Joseph Stiglitz warned that current AI investment is a "bubble" built on unsustainable foundations, asserting that AI will assist human labor rather than replace jobs on a large scale. In response to global trade shifts, Korea's Ministry of Industry is establishing a new unit to manage strategic investments in the U.S., focusing on key sectors like AI, shipbuilding, and pharmaceuticals. There are concerns that AI-driven labor market changes could disproportionately impact younger generations by reducing hiring, rather than leading to mass layoffs, emphasizing the need for flexible employment and more experience-building opportunities.
sections.Others: Government support for long-term care insurance in Korea quadrupled over the past decade to 2.5 trillion KRW last year, reflecting the nation's rapidly aging population. The increase aligns with legal requirements for state funding equivalent to 20% of expected annual insurance premiums, supporting active senior lives. In international political news, the U.S. is reportedly considering deploying special forces to secure Iran's enriched uranium, which currently amounts to enough for 11 nuclear bombs, indicating escalating tensions. Discussions also touch upon the concept of "ghost GDP" arising from oversupply and the need for high-performance, domain-specific AI models to boost Korean industries like manufacturing and finance.
